title: Install Profiles
description: Named install shapes for a consumer repository, expressed as sets of components rather than as lists of files. The indirection is the point: a profile says what a repository is for, a component says which files serve that purpose, and adding a file to the system therefore updates one component instead of every profile that happens to want it.

profiles.description: The install shapes, keyed by profile name. Kept few on purpose. A long menu of profiles reads as flexibility and behaves as a decision the installer cannot make, and profiles nobody chooses still have to be tested and kept working.

description.description: Which repository this profile is for, stated as a situation rather than as a feature list, so a person choosing between profiles can recognise their own repository in one of them.

components.description: Component names to install. Every entry must be a key in the top-level `components` map; a profile naming a component that does not exist installs less than it claims and says nothing about it.
What each component name resolves to, keyed by component name. Values are repository-relative paths; a trailing slash means the whole directory.

hookProfileDefault.description: The hook profile an install starts at. It must be one of the three the runtime recognises — an unrecognised value falls back to standard rather than to off, because a typo in a config value must never silently disable every gate in the system.

note.description: Free text for the rules a shape cannot express — here, that a profile is a starting point rather than a cage, that the installer accepts additions and removals on top of one, and that the resolved set is recorded in the install state so a repair can reproduce the original intent instead of guessing from what happens to be on disk.
